sets.relationshipLabel: a place and the activity it exists for
sets.explanation: A locksmith shop exists to cut keys, and a vault exists to keep things safe — each place is defined by its one purpose.

sets.relationshipLabel: broad category and a specific kind of thing within it
sets.explanation: A deadbolt is one kind of lock, and a skeleton key is one kind of key — each pair moves from the general class to a named variety.

sets.relationshipLabel: the start and end of a process or career
sets.explanation: An apprentice becomes a master, and an installed part eventually gets replaced — each pair traces a beginning to its eventual end.

sets.relationshipLabel: a lock mechanism and the internal part that defines its function
sets.explanation: A plug turns because of its pins, and a warded lock works because of its ward — each mechanism is defined by the hidden part inside it.

glossary.definition: An old style opening mechanism worked by a notched metal piece that must slip past internal obstacles shaped just so.

definitions.definition: A little storefront where someone makes keys and fixes locks for a living.
Grinding a blank piece of metal into the exact shape needed to work a particular lock.
A heavy, reinforced room or box built to keep valuables locked away and untouched.
Holding onto something carefully so nothing happens to it while it's in your care.
A device that keeps something shut until the right key or code opens it.
A sturdy lock bolt that slides straight into the frame for extra security on a door.
A small shaped piece of metal made to open one particular lock.
A simplified key filed down so it can open many different old-style locks.
Someone learning a trade by working under and watching a skilled person.
Someone who's fully learned a trade and can do it expertly on their own.
Putting something new in place and getting it set up to work.
Taking out something worn or broken and putting a fresh one in its place.
The rotating core inside a lock that turns when the right key is inserted.
A tiny spring-loaded piece inside a lock that has to line up just right to let it turn.
An old style opening mechanism worked by a notched metal piece that must slip past internal obstacles shaped just so.
A fixed obstruction inside an old lock that blocks any key that isn't cut to match it.
